messages:
Morgan: Morning — quick Q for today's handoff (11:30). Can we lock down who owns what during non-incident coverage? I'll be swapping with Alex and want clear bullets for the notes.
Alex: @Morgan short version: SRE = infra-level alerts (hosts, k8s node pressure, network flaps, cloud limits). Runtime = model-serving surface (decode errors, KV/cache corruption, token-level latency regressions, model OOMs). For anything that looks like customer-facing degradation, call pager.
Sam: Adding a couple of concrete rules we've used:
- 5xx from gateway/middleware -> SRE first (likely infra or routing).
- End-to-end elevated p95 latency for generation (not just infra queue) -> runtime.
- Model quality regressions (e.g., hallucinations, major output changes) -> runtime + product notify.
Rachel: To align on "incident" definition: treat something as an incident if it meets any of these: customer-facing outage for >10% of requests, persistent errors for >10 minutes, data loss/exposure, or contractual SLA breach. Otherwise it's an operational FYI or alert to monitor. Use Incident Bot for SEV declarations.
Alex: Quick escalation matrix (feel free to paste into handoff notes):
```
1) Triage thread with initial findings + screenshots/logs.
2) If customer impact or sustained errors -> declare SEV in Incident Bot and call SRE pager.
3) If model decode/OOM/KV issue -> add runtime pager and link model run_id.
4) If unsure -> page both teams and assign temporary owner.
```
Morgan: Good. What about ownership of rollbacks/fallbacks? E.g., if a newfound model regression appears in prod, who flips fallback routes?
Alex: Runtime should flip model-level fallbacks (variant switch, model pin). SRE should only intervene for infra-level rollbacks (node pools, networking, infra autoscaler). If it's cross-cutting, coordinate in the thread and nominate a single executor.
Sam: Also: please include these quick log snippets in handoff so the oncoming engineer can run the right commands: `kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide`, `tail -n 200 /var/log/runtime/serve.log | grep ERROR`, and our internal trace link pattern `https://traces.redwood.io/{trace_id}`.
Oncall Bot: Reminder: upcoming handoff at 11:30. Next oncall window: 11:30-19:30. Use `/incident declare` if escalating.
Rachel: One more FYI — if you see a capacity regen event (GPUs cycling) treat as infra-first; capacity events often mask as model timeouts.
Morgan: Perfect, thanks all. I'll paste this into the official handoff note and add explicit "who pings who" lines. Will @here at 11:25 to kick off the swap.
Sam: +1
Alex: Thanks — I'll be available for the first 15 minutes after swap for any quick handover questions.
